provenance: Read retained eight-page conference paper and enlarged tables. Historical 2008/2009 sources, not current law. No native numerical actuarial/reservoir model or calibration. Synthetic examples are explicitly analyst choices outside accepted Paper 1 inputs.

quotes.handoff: these rules require monitoring but do not have any provisions for a transfer of responsibility
quotes.performance: post-injection site care will continue until the plume is stabilized and cannot endanger USDWs
quotes.longer_version: A longer version of this paper can be found in the Emory Law Review, Fall 2008.

phases.name: active_injection
phases.author_proposal: Operator liability and insurance, central-fund contribution during injection.

phases.name: postclosure
phases.author_proposal: Operator monitoring, verification, remediation and full damage liability, with financial assurance; pool design must address moral hazard.

phases.name: long_term_stewardship
phases.author_proposal: After predetermined performance conditions and sufficient funding, public or hybrid stewardship supports monitoring/remediation/damages and data/site management.

analyst.scope: Two Bernoulli site losses and mixture correlation are synthetic, not observed CCS hazards. Funding example uses three end-year deposits, constant postclosure monitoring and no damage/remediation payments; no native fee/insurance premium/physical injection service inferred.
